Select a parsimonious nnet model

Source: R/select-nnet.R
select_nnet.Rd

select_nnet() implements the information-criterion procedure of McInerney and Burke. It first selects the hidden-layer size, applies backward input selection, and then alternates one-step changes to the hidden and input layers. Each candidate is fitted from several random initialisations using nnet::nnet().

Usage

select_nnet(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'formula'
select_nnet(
  x,
  data,
  ...,
  max_size,
  n_starts = 5L,
  criterion = c("BIC", "AIC", "AICc"),
  start_range = c(-3, 3),
  maxit = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  progress = TRUE
)

# Default S3 method
select_nnet(
  x,
  y,
  ...,
  max_size,
  n_starts = 5L,
  criterion = c("BIC", "AIC", "AICc"),
  start_range = c(-3, 3),
  maxit = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A model formula or a numeric design matrix.

...

Arguments passed to methods and then to nnet::nnet(). Arguments that would change the supported architecture, response model, initial weights, or decay value are not allowed.

data

A data frame used with the formula interface.

max_size

Maximum number of hidden units considered in the initial hidden-layer search.

n_starts

Number of random initialisations fitted for each candidate.

criterion

Information criterion used to compare candidates.

start_range

Numeric vector of length two giving the lower and upper bounds for uniformly generated starting weights.

maxit

Maximum number of nnet optimiser iterations per start.

seed

Optional random seed for reproducible starting weights.

progress

Whether to print progress as candidate models are fitted.

y

A numeric response used with the matrix interface.

Value

An object of class "statnnet_selection" containing the selected native nnet fit, selected terms or columns, the full search path, and start-level convergence diagnostics.

Details

Selection is available for unpenalised Gaussian regression. With a formula, complete right-hand-side terms are selected together: all columns belonging to a factor or transformed term enter or leave as a group. With a matrix, columns are selected individually.

References

McInerney, A. and Burke, K. (2025). A statistical modelling approach to feedforward neural network model selection. Statistical Modelling, 25(4), 323–342. doi:10.1177/1471082X241258261 .

Examples

set.seed(1)
example_data <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(60), x2 = rnorm(60))
example_data$y <- 1 + 2 * example_data$x1 + rnorm(60, sd = 0.4)

selection <- select_nnet(
  y ~ x1 + x2,
  data = example_data,
  max_size = 1,
  n_starts = 2,
  maxit = 500,
  seed = 2,
  progress = FALSE
)
selection
#> statnnet model selection
#> Call:
#> select_nnet(x = y ~ x1 + x2, data = example_data, max_size = 1, 
#>     n_starts = 2, maxit = 500, seed = 2, progress = FALSE)
#> Selected model: 1 input column, 1 hidden unit, 4 network weights
#> BIC: 81.590; 5 candidate models; 10 converged starts
#> Selected terms: x1
#> Excluded terms: x2
